scene.title: Aral Sea shoreline retreat
scene.description: Real satellite comparison of the South Aral Sea. The eastern basin is visibly smaller and largely dry in the later image. This is contextual source information, not a classification produced by TerraLens.
caveats: Some clouds near the upper left in the baseline.
Seasonal surface color, residual registration, atmospheric differences, and changing water color can create candidate differences.
MODIS browse imagery is regional-scale; not suitable for claims about individual roads or buildings.
scene.georeferencing: Exact output bounds specified in the NASA GIBS WMS 1.1.1 request; north-up, linear longitude/latitude raster. Service geolocation is not independently surveyed.
scene.alignment: Both dates rendered by GIBS to identical projection, bounds, and dimensions; visually checked stable terrain. No independent subpixel registration validation.

files.preparation: Converted GIBS PNG to RGB JPEG quality 94. No geometric edits, invented overlays, or content replacement.

preparation: Original shipped JPEGs decoded by Pillow; bilinear resize only when longest edge exceeds 768. Lake Mead is an independent NASA GIBS PNG pair. Browser Canvas decoding can differ slightly.

findings.summary: Analysis identified 34 visual-change regions, covering 19.25% of valid processing pixels. 47.4% of detected change pixels lie in the center third of the north-up scene. The largest region contains 100,175 changed pixels. These are preliminary visual findings requiring evidence inspection. Sensitive to threshold selection.
limitations: RGB differences describe appearance, not cause or operational significance. No automatic object or terrain classification is applied.
Lighting, shadows, seasonal variation, clouds and residual misalignment may affect results; clouds and shadows are not automatically detected.
Region sizes refer to the processing grid, not geographic area. Small or low-contrast changes may be missed.
Coordinates use supplied north-up geographic bounds; geolocation is not independently verified.

reliability.reason: 99,611 pixels persist across all tested thresholds; 18,958 appear only at the lowest threshold (highest tested sensitivity).
reliability.method: Pixel-mask intersection across three thresholds, after identical minimum-area filtering. The stable label requires intersection/union ≥ 0.80 (heuristic). Per-region labels require ≥ 80% of that region's pixels to persist. Neither ratio is confidence or accuracy. Region identity is not matched across runs.

limitations: Quality screening is heuristic and not a validated image-quality or registration score.
The shift screen tests only integer translations within ±4 processing pixels; rotation, scale, subpixel displacement, perspective, and local distortions remain unchecked.

scene.title: Indus floodplain change
scene.description: Real satellite comparison during the August 2022 Pakistan floods. Water-related visual changes are evident around the Indus floodplain. This is contextual source information, not a classification produced by TerraLens.
caveats: Both dates contain clouds and cloud shadows; these must not be interpreted automatically as terrain change.
False-color rendered imagery, not raw spectral reflectance.
VIIRS regional-scale visualization cannot establish road passability or individual building damage.
